description: Core's TraversalPlanner, VehicleRegistry and FastTravelDirector wired together with a StaminaPool and the personal vehicles, with no Prolog engine (every permission granted, every authored requirement unmet), a recording bus, a scripted geometry probe (input.probe: link id → passable; a link not listed is unanswered) and a scripted locomotion host (input.locomotion.stuck: destination → where the host leaves the actor). Each step's output pins the reports, the orders the host was given, the clock advances, the vehicles' states and the bus events.
runner: src/traversal/systems-corpus.ts (runTraversalSystemsOp). Compare exactly, object key sets included; an unknown op or step is an error.
regenerate: npm run traversal-systems-corpus; npm run traversal-systems-corpus:check fails on any difference.

cases.name: a-walk-charges-the-shared-meter-and-the-host-is-told-one-order
cases.note: The decision layer end to end: the affordances out of the camp (refused ones kept, with why), the cheapest route across (the swim, conditional on its rope), then a walk. The meter is 120's energy, charged the link's cost scaled by the mode (4 walked = 4); the locomotion host gets exactly one order and core learns one arrival; the bus hears traversal_completed once.

cases.name: negative-an-authored-requirement-is-unmet-with-no-kb-so-the-swim-is-refused
cases.note: The swim across is conditional (has_item(rope, 1)). With no KB core cannot meet an authored goal, so the attempt is refused `requires` and names the goal; nothing is charged, nobody moves, no event. The boat on the same edge is refused `mode` (wren cannot row).

cases.name: the-host-geometry-refuses-the-jump-and-an-unanswered-link-is-passable
cases.note: The jump from the ford is a geometric link: the probe is asked once per attempt. Answered false it is refused `impassable`; a geometric link nobody answered for is passable (a corpus or a turn-based game must not have every jump refused).

cases.name: a-geometric-link-nobody-answered-for-is-crossed-once-the-actor-can-jump
cases.note: Refused `mode` while wren can only walk; once the host says wren can jump (movement_mode/2 through setModes), the unanswered geometric link is crossed; the climb on is refused `mode` again.

cases.name: negative-an-almost-empty-meter-refuses-the-climb-and-charges-nothing
cases.note: A climb of 5 costs 15 (climb × 3). With 14 left it is refused `stamina` and the meter keeps its 14.

cases.name: the-host-could-not-carry-the-order-out-and-the-actor-is-where-the-host-left-them
cases.note: arrived false: the actor is put where the host reported, the event says so, and the walk was still charged (the attempt happened).

cases.name: board-take-the-reins-row-to-the-island-and-get-off-the-skiff
cases.note: The vehicle verbs through the registry: boarding the skiff where wren stands, taking the reins lends `boat`, the order to the host names the vehicle, the skiff follows its driver across, and getting off hands the reins and the mode back. (The far bank is not rowed to: its edge carries the swim’s rope requirement, which no KB meets.) The skiff is the ferryman's; with no KB nothing forbids taking it.

cases.name: negative-the-vehicle-verbs-refuse-in-their-ladder-order
cases.note: An unknown vehicle; the cart is at the ford, not the camp (`elsewhere`); the reins without being aboard (`not_aboard`); boarding twice (`redundant`); a second driver (`occupied`); a third rider for two seats (`full`); getting off what one never boarded (`not_aboard`).

cases.name: a-fast-travel-passes-world-time-in-bounded-advances-and-counts-the-journey
cases.note: Only a discovered place is offered and only along a way the traveller could walk. The ridge costs 4 + 3×2 + 5×3 = 25, so 25 hours in four 6-hour advances and a 1-hour remainder, handed to the clock in order before the arrival; the journey ordinal rises, so the same trip again draws differently (pinned in fast-travel.json); the bus hears fast_travel_completed once.

cases.name: negative-fast-travel-refuses-undiscovered-same-place-and-unreachable
cases.note: In FAST_TRAVEL_REFUSALS order: where the traveller already is; the watchtower never found; the ridge once a landslide closes the only climb. Nothing advances the clock.

cases.name: negative-a-journey-along-a-conditional-route-is-refused-for-its-goal-with-no-kb
cases.note: The far bank is reached only by the swim, whose edge asks for a rope. With no KB the goal is unmet, so the journey is refused `requires` and names it; the plan (and its hours) is still reported.

cases.name: a-horse-lends-ride-so-the-meadow-trail-opens-and-getting-off-closes-it
cases.note: The personal vehicle (Babylon's B key) in the same session: the meadow trail is a `ride` link, refused `mode` on foot. Mounting the horse lends `ride` through the planner, the walk factor is 3000 (×3), and the trail opens; the bicycle lends nothing, so cycling on to on foot closes it again. vehicle_mounted / vehicle_dismounted are what the host raises on the bus (mountEvents).

cases.name: negative-nobody-aboard-the-skiff-gets-on-a-horse-but-a-rider-may-always-get-off
cases.note: The one rung where the two kinds of vehicle meet: aboard the skiff, mounting is refused `in_vehicle` (naming the skiff); a rider who boarded on horseback may still get off the horse, and the skiff's `boat` stays with whoever holds its reins.

cases.name: a-save-taken-mid-playthrough-loads-back-every-layer-as-it-was
cases.note: The traversal block written from the four layers' state, the playthrough moves on (a row to the island, the skiff left there, the bicycle put away, the landslide cleared, the ridge found), and the block is loaded back (a load step with no block loads the last save step’s): every layer serializes as it did at the save, silently (a load raises no event), and the skiff is back at the camp with its driver.

cases.name: negative-an-actor-nobody-registered-is-nowhere
cases.note: An unregistered actor has no location: the traversal is `unreachable` and no order is given; mounting still works (a personal vehicle has no place) but there are no modes to lend to.

cases.name: the-bus-names-who-got-on-and-off-the-cart-and-a-horse
cases.note: PL.vehicle-events (U90(4)): vehicle_mounted / vehicle_dismounted carry an optional actorId (absent means the player), and core names it for any actor. Boarding the cart raises vehicle_mounted with the cart's id as vehicleType after vehicle_state_changed, getting off raises vehicle_dismounted, and taking the reins raises no second mount. The villager ash and wren are told apart on the bus, on the cart and on their personal vehicles (mountEvents and events).

cases.name: a-boatman-who-holds-boat-of-his-own-keeps-it-after-giving-up-the-skiff
cases.note: PL.vehicle-events (U90(5)): the reins lend only a mode the driver does not already hold. bec holds `boat` of his own, so taking the skiff's reins lends nothing and getting off leaves him `boat`; wren held no `boat`, so the skiff lends it (lent by vehicle:skiff, shown in the save) and getting off takes it back.

cases.name: a-rider-who-holds-ride-of-their-own-keeps-it-off-the-horse
cases.note: PL.vehicle-events (U90(5)), the personal vehicle: wren holds `ride` of her own, so the horse lends nothing and getting off leaves her `ride` (the meadow trail stays open); ash held no `ride`, so getting off the horse takes back what it lent.

cases.name: the-carts-reins-keep-ride-after-the-horse-is-gone-and-the-horse-keeps-it-after-the-cart
cases.note: PL.vehicle-events (U90(5)), both kinds of vehicle lending one mode: on horseback wren boards the cart and takes its reins, so `ride` is lent by both (personal:horse, vehicle:cart). Getting off the horse leaves `ride` to the cart's reins and getting off the cart takes it; the other way round, getting off the cart leaves `ride` to the horse and getting off the horse takes it.

cases.name: a-save-keeps-which-modes-were-lent-so-getting-off-after-a-load-gives-back-the-same
cases.note: PL.vehicle-events (U90(5)): the planner row carries `lent` in the save, so after a load a rider who held `ride` of her own (wren) still keeps it off the horse and one the horse lent it to (ash) still loses it, exactly as without the load.
